lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: We have more ways to talk to each other than ever before. And yet Britain and Japan both decided they needed a minister for loneliness.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The World Health Organization says one in six people worldwide is affected by loneliness. America's Surgeon General compared its risk of early death to smoking up to fifteen cigarettes a day.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Americans went from about an hour a day with friends in 2003 to twenty minutes in 2020. And far more of us live alone.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Add self-checkouts, food left at the door and phones in every hand, and modern life looks guilty.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: But it's murkier than that. Studies tracking loneliness over decades find small rises at most. And people in poorer countries report about twice the loneliness of people in rich ones.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Even the phone debate is unsettled. One big Oxford study found screen use was linked to teen wellbeing about as much as eating potatoes.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: Nobody's writing a bestseller about potatoes.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: What nobody disputes is that connection matters. Harvard's study of adult life, running since 1938, found good relationships keep people happier and healthier.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So modern life doesn't force us to be lonely. It just no longer forces us not to be. The full story is on our channel.
